title: Melon Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Melon Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Melon nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, potassium and magnesium in milon, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Melon nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your milon (melon) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, potassium, magnesium, molybdenum, calcium, boron and phosphorus. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Nitrogen deficiency on a leaf, shown on another crop as a stand in for melon
heroImage.credit: Maja Dumat, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, magnesium, molybdenum and phosphorus move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But calcium and boron stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which melon nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.
Melon nutrient deficiency signs, old leaves and young leaves
Shows first on the old leaves

blocks.caption: Deficiencies that start on the young leaves of milon

New leaves crinkle and hook, vine tips die, and fruits are small, soft or tasteless.

Young fruits drop, and fruits show yellow streaks, corky marks and cracks.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a melon nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest melon nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in melon

Older leaves turn pale to light green, yellow and drop, and the yellowing moves up the shoot. Vines are stunted and fruits are pale, small and misshapen, so yield falls. You see it most at this stage: vine growth and fruit set.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in milon
Sandy soils, heavy rain or irrigation, low organic matter, and no side dressing before fruit set.
How to tell it apart

Magnesium shortage, very common in melon, leaves the veins green on old leaves. Molybdenum shortage on acid soil shows pale crown leaves at vining. To be sure, old leaves yellow first. Soil test and leaf tissue test.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency
Side dress urea or ammonium sulfate based on the soil test, before the fruits form. For a quick fix, give a urea leaf spray at 10 grams per liter of water every 15 days for Cucumis melo.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, add manure and split nitrogen.
Potassium deficiency in melon

Older leaves yellow and scorch, cup and curl upward, with sunken dead spots along the midrib. Vines die back, stems weaken and fewer female flowers form. Fruits can be spotted, off flavoured and less sweet. You see it most at this stage: fruit filling. Melon uses more potassium than nitrogen and most of it moves from the leaves into the fruit.
Why potassium deficiency happens in milon
Sandy or acid soils, heavy rain, and too little potash during fruit filling.
How to tell it apart
Magnesium shortage yellows between the veins first. Potassium burns the edges first. To be sure, soil test for potassium and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for potassium deficiency
Apply muriate of potash or sulfate of potash based on the soil test, in split doses. For immediate relief, give a morning spray of sulfate of potash at 10 grams per liter of water with a sticker.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, give potash at planting and again at fruit set, and keep potassium, calcium and magnesium in balance.
Magnesium deficiency in melon

Yellowing between the veins starts on the oldest leaves and moves up the vine. Yellow tissue may brown, die and drop out, leaving a shot hole look, or turn red with spotted dead patches. Older leaves drop early and yield falls. The University of Kentucky says muskmelon shows this more than other cucurbits. You see it most at this stage: fast growth while the fruits enlarge.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in milon
Sandy soils with low holding capacity, low pH, dry years, and heavy potash, lime or ammonium fertilizer.
How to tell it apart

Manganese toxicity on very acid soil can look like it, with water soaked areas under the leaves and yellow or bronze spots on top. A soil pH test tells them apart. To be sure, soil test for magnesium, potassium and pH, and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

The University of Kentucky advises keeping pH near 6.5 and feeding Epsom salt through drip lines if needed. Leaf sprays rarely fix a serious shortage. Give magnesium sulfate in a band near the plants at about 80 kg per hectare (32 kg per acre) for Cucumis melo. Do not apply magnesium with potash.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **YaraTera KRISTA MgS** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (16 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur), **Magnepro** by Ramgo International Corporation (16 percent MgO and 12.8 percent sulfur) and **Lucky Planters Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate (Epsom Salt)** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (16.27 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, apply dolomitic lime before planting on acid soil and avoid heavy potassium, calcium or ammonium fertilizer.
Molybdenum deficiency in melon

Leaves near the crown turn pale green to slightly yellow between the veins around the time plants begin to vine. As it worsens, leaf edges and areas between veins burn and die, and growth stops. Other cucurbits on the same soil often show no signs. You see it most at this stage: start of vining.
Why molybdenum deficiency happens in milon
Heavy soils with pH below 6, and heavy ammonium fertilizer through drip lines, which acidifies the root zone and can also bring manganese toxicity.
How to tell it apart

Nitrogen shortage yellows old leaves evenly. Magnesium shortage starts on the oldest leaves and comes later, during fruiting. To be sure, soil pH test. NSW DPI suggests spraying a few plants with sodium molybdate and checking for normal, greener growth.
What to apply for molybdenum deficiency

The University of Kentucky advises leaf sprays of sodium molybdate and keeping pH at 6.0 to 6.5. NSW DPI gives about 50 grams of sodium molybdate in 100 liters of water as a leaf spray, or about 1 kg per hectare mixed with fertilizer before the next crop.

Sold here with molybdenum: **Tierramino Molybdenum** by Unilox Far East Resources Inc. (16 percent molybdenum), **YaraVita Teprosyn Mo** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (15 percent P2O5 and 15.3 percent molybdenum), **Biozome** by Manchem Industries, Inc. (12 percent S, 12 percent Zn, 3 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 1 percent Fe, 1 percent Cu, 0.5 percent B, 0.05 percent Mo) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate General Purpose** by Sagrex Corporation (2 percent Fe, 0.5 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 3 percent S with Cu, Zn, B, Mo). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [molybdenum deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/molybdenum-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid soil to pH 6 to 6.5 ahead of planting and avoid heavy ammonium feeding.
Calcium deficiency in melon

Young leaves show yellow stripes beside the midrib, crinkle, yellow at the edges and become brittle, and the spaces between leaves shorten. Growing tips die back and roots are stunted. Fruits may be small and tasteless or fail to form. You see it most at this stage: vine growth and early fruiting.
Why calcium deficiency happens in milon
Very acid soils, uneven watering, excess phosphorus and low boron. Only a small share of the plant's calcium reaches the fruit, so steady water matters.
How to tell it apart
Boron shortage also deforms new growth and drops young fruit. To be sure, soil test for calcium, pH and boron.
What to apply for calcium deficiency
Try lime at about 250 kg per hectare when soil pH is 5.5 to 6, or about 840 kg per hectare in two doses when pH is 3.5 to 4.5. Gypsum on soil that is not acid. Water evenly.

Sold here with calcium: **Planters Products Lifelime** by Planters Products, Inc. (50.59 percent CaO), **Macrock Limestone** by Donumdei 1 Corp. (36 to 42 percent calcium), **Calcic Lime** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (35.52 percent calcium) and **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer for tomatoes](/blog/fertilizer-for-tomatoes), and the page on [calcium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/calcium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime before planting and keep calcium, potassium and magnesium in balance.
Boron deficiency in melon

New leaves are malformed and the plant becomes bushy as buds die. Young fruits drop or abort, and fruits show yellow streaks and corky skin marks. Mature fruits may be small, light or cracked. You see it most at this stage: flowering and fruit set.
Why boron deficiency happens in milon
Sandy soils, overlimed soils, low organic matter and drought.
How to tell it apart
Poor pollination also drops young fruits but leaves stay normal. To be sure, soil test for boron and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for boron deficiency

Try borax in the soil at about 10 kg per hectare (4 kg per acre) or a borax spray at 1 gram per liter of water. Delaware lists muskmelon among crops with a medium boron need, about 2 pounds of boron per acre before planting. Do not mix borax with calcium or ammonium fertilizer.

Sold here with boron: **Solubor** by Caldic Philippines Inc. (21 percent boron), **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (11 percent boron), **YaraVita BORTRAC 150** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (11.1 percent boron) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate Boron** by Sagrex Corporation (10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, add a small boron dose to the basal fertilizer on sandy fields.
Phosphorus deficiency in melon

Leaves turn purple, especially along the veins. Shoots are short and thin, young leaves are small, stiff and dark green, and leaves look dull and shrivelled. Vigour, fruit set and yield are poor. You see it most at this stage: early growth, and from flowering to fruit fill, when melon needs the most phosphorus.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in milon
Acid or iron rich soils, low organic matter, cold or waterlogged soil, and no phosphorus at planting.
How to tell it apart
Root knot nematodes also stunt vines. To be sure, soil test for available phosphorus and pH.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency
Apply phosphorus in the hill based on the soil test. Use single superphosphate for a quick fix. Uptake is best near pH 6.2 to 7.0.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use complete fertilizer or 16 20 0 in the hill at planting.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any melon nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your milon needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Melon nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my milon leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: old leaves pale and yellow up the vine, and fruits are small and misshapen. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at magnesium deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in melon?
items.a: Side dress urea or ammonium sulfate based on the soil test, before the fruits form. For a quick fix, give a urea leaf spray at 10 grams per liter of water every 15 days for Cucumis melo.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in melon?
items.a: Apply muriate of potash or sulfate of potash based on the soil test, in split doses. For immediate relief, give a morning spray of sulfate of potash at 10 grams per liter of water with a sticker.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes magnesium deficiency in melon?
items.a: The University of Kentucky advises keeping pH near 6.5 and feeding Epsom salt through drip lines if needed. Leaf sprays rarely fix a serious shortage.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my milon lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the melon nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
